title: Debugging Lisp: fix and resume a program from any point in the stack - how Common Lisp stands out.
summary: A five-minute demo of the Common Lisp debugger fixing a bug, recompiling a single function, and resuming execution from the failed stack frame. It shows how to avoid re-running long computations.
why: HN Lisp fans repeatedly link it as a short, concrete demonstration of Common Lisp's interactive debugging advantage.

quote.text: my demo to show how to resume execution of a long running program, from the stack frame right before the bug
